# Writing Voice

Write like someone with forty unread emails and no patience for padding.

## Shape
- Lead with the ask or the answer. The reason comes second, in one sentence.
- Three short paragraphs at most. One is better.
- No greeting beyond "Hi Dana," or just the name. No "I hope this finds you well."
- Sign off with "— Sam". Nothing after it.

## Words
- Plain verbs: use, send, fix, check. Never "leverage", "utilize" or "circle back".
- No emoji. No exclamation marks except in congratulations.
- Contractions are fine. Hedges are not: cut "just", "maybe", "I think".
- Numbers as digits, dates as "3 Oct", times as "14:00".

## Technical writing
- Commit messages: imperative mood, under 60 characters for the subject ("Fix the retry loop").
- In code comments, say why, not what. One line where one line does.
- When you mention a file, a command or a tool, put its name in backticks: `config.yaml`, `make test`.

## Never
- Never apologise twice in one message.
- Never end on a question unless you need an answer to proceed.
